To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the HRQL of food allergic patients is significantly impaired compared to the general population and that food allergic patients are at a higher risk of developing psychiatric disorders.

food allergic patients experience a significantly lower quality of life than non-allergic individuals and that this lower quality of life can be attributed to the food allergy itself and the food allergy-related interventions.
food allergy has a significant negative impact on HRQL and that this impact can be significantly reduced by food allergy-related interventions.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following topics: (i) HRQL instruments in food allergy; (ii) the impact of food avoidance on HRQL; (iii) the impact of allergen avoidance on HRQL in food-allergic patients; (iv) the impact of oral immunotherapy on HRQL in patients with food allergy; (v) the impact of psychological factors on HRQL in children with food allergy; and (vi) the impact of quality of care on HRQL in adolescents with food allergy.

the impact of food allergies on patients’ HRQL, the effect of allergen avoidance strategies on HRQL, the influence of food-allergic patients’ coping strategies on their HRQL, and the role of HRQL in the decision-making process regarding food allergy management.
